reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes paid trading packages whose advertised earnings depend on recruiting people into left-and-right teams and qualifying through multiple downline ranks. It encourages participation with claims of substantial weekly and monthly income, bonuses, prizes, and token-related gains, while directing viewers toward increasingly expensive packages and emphasizing rapid growth. The income disclaimer does not change that the main communication is an active recruitment and earnings solicitation.

opening.argument: The material expressly presents itself as live training about digital currency, not as a promise that every viewer will profit. Most importantly, the speaker gives an explicit income disclosure: “this is no guarantee that you're going to make the same kind of money” and explains that results depend on effort, commitment, and ability. That qualification materially changes the meaning of the earnings examples: they are conditional illustrations within a business presentation, not guaranteed outcomes. The content therefore supports an educational, risk-qualified interpretation rather than a deceptive certification of returns.

citations.quote: The Crypto Pro's Live Training With Alan C Delaney
this is no guarantee that you're going to make the same kind of money
the money that you make is based on your effort, based on your commitment, and based on your abilities

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes selected high earnings figures, but those figures are immediately qualified by the speaker's express no-guarantee disclosure. Its quoted 40% allocation describes where compensation is placed, not a guaranteed investment return. Likewise, mentioning a 5,000 euro package and possible weekly maximum does not establish that viewers were promised those results; the speaker expressly says outcomes vary.

citations.quote: some people will make a lot more than what I am sharing with you and some people will make a lot less
40% goes into like your trading account

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer does not neutralize the presentation's central inducement. The speaker still describes qualification through a person on each side and gives concrete commission examples tied to personally referred packages. Saying results vary cannot make a compensation structure based on recruiting and downline volume into ordinary risk education.

opening.argument: The format is a worked explanation of how a digital-currency business model operates. It walks through package upgrades, rank qualifications, point balances, weekly limits, matching calculations, and the division between cash and trading accounts. Those examples are presented as demonstrations of the plan's mechanics, including arithmetic such as a smaller-side volume producing a stated bonus. Explaining how a system calculates rewards is not by itself proof that the presenter is soliciting a viewer or certifying the system's safety. The title and description also frame the material as live training and learning about digital currency.

The balance for the next week is zero points on your left and there's 1,400 points that rolls over to the next week.
the matching bonuses works like this

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution calls the explanation solicitation, but the cited material can equally be read as a tutorial showing how the plan calculates volume, ranks, and bonuses. Describing the mechanics, including examples of package amounts and token allocation, does not itself prove a deceptive claim or a demand that the audience join. The content's instructional structure matters.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial framing does not erase what is being taught. The explanation specifically instructs participants where to place people, urges focus on the lower-volume side, and connects personally referred people to matching income. Those are operational recruitment instructions, not merely neutral arithmetic or digital-currency education.

opening.argument: At its most concrete, the material describes packages, bonuses, ranks, and an account allocation within a promoted business service. It does not show a request for passwords, identity documents, or other credentials, and the supplied material does not establish a guaranteed return or a particular viewer's required payment. The description presents the subject as learning about named digital currencies, while the compensation discussion explains what the service's packages and referral rewards are said to provide. That is consistent with ordinary commercial promotion and referral compensation; the evidence alone does not establish that the underlying service is fraudulent.

these are the different packages that people can purchase now
60% of your income goes into your cash account and 40% of your income goes into your trading account

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution infers a scam from the existence of packages and referrals, but referral compensation and tiered rewards can occur in legitimate commercial programs. Its quoted examples show what the presenter says the plan pays, not proof that money was taken unlawfully or that a return was guaranteed. The supplied evidence does not establish deception, credential harvesting, or a failed product.

That recruitment-dependent structure is the relevant mechanism, even without a password request or an explicit guarantee.
